ANSWER TO COMMENTS OF THE INDEPENDENT MARKET MONITOR FOR PJM
            Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”),1 the Applicants2 respectfully submit this

motion for leave to answer and answer (“Answer”) to the comments by the Independent Market

Monitor (“IMM”) for PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) filed on the Application (“IMM

Comments”).3 The IMM Comments seek the imposition of a condition that would limit the

removal of certain of the Applicants from the PJM capacity market for the purpose of providing

“direct” service power supply to data centers.4

           The IMM Comments seek relief that is far beyond the scope of the Commission’s

evaluation of the Proposed Transaction, represent a collateral attack on prior Commission orders,

and cannot properly be granted by the Commission. Accordingly, the Applicants reiterate their

request for prompt Commission authorization, including the issuance of an order by November 20,

2026, or as soon thereafter as is practicable.

I.         MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER

           Applicants respectfully move for leave to file this Answer and request that the Commission

accept this Answer. This Answer clarifies the issues raised by the IMM comments and provides

information that will assist the Commission in its decision-making process.

           Although the Commission’s rules generally prohibit answers to protests or comments,5 the

Commission permits an answer when it provides useful and relevant information that will assist

II.       ANSWER

          The IMM Comments incorrectly imply that the Proposed Transaction presents some basis

for special scrutiny by the Commission that, in turn, would justify the imposition on the Applicants

of the IMM’s demand for a highly unusual condition on closing. The IMM posits that “[t]he

impact on competition and reliability of the massive and sudden growth of load from data centers

is the most critical issue affecting PJM markets and the public interest in competitive outcomes

today.”7 The IMM then assumes without support that “every owner of capacity [within PJM is]

pivotal.”8 From these unsupported hypotheses, the IMM asserts that the Proposed Transaction

requires an extraordinary and undefined condition that the Commission has affirmatively rejected

in other, recent, transactions subject to FPA Section 203.9

          A.       The Proposed Transaction Fully Satisfies the Requirements of 18 C.F.R. §
                   2.26.

          Section 2.26 of the Commission’s regulations sets forth the Commission’s policies

concerning the review of applications under FPA Section 203.10               As demonstrated in the

Application and in the Solomon and Opgrand Affidavit, the Proposed Transaction satisfies each

 element of the Commission’s Section 203 framework in 18 C.F.R. § 2.26. Matters unrelated to

those statutory and regulatory criteria fall outside the Commission’s transaction-specific review.

            The Application fully addresses the competition, rate, regulatory, and cross-subsidization

standards set forth in Section 2.26 of the Commission’s regulations. The IMM Comments do not

assert that the Proposed Transaction fails to satisfy those requirements. The IMM Comments also

effectively acknowledge11 that the Proposed Transaction is statistically insignificant within PJM:

the combination of 543 MW (including conservatively assumed potential future capacity) and 938

MW of generating capacity, totalling 1,481 MW,12 amounts to less than one percent of PJM’s total

installed capacity. Prior to the closing of the Proposed Transaction, each of the Purchaser and the

Seller is affiliated with less than one percent of PJM’s installed capacity. Following closing, the

Purchaser and EDF Spring Field WPC, LLC (“EDF Spring Field); Fox Squirrel Solar LLC (“Fox

Squirrel”); Kelly Creek Wind, LLC (“Kelly Creek”); and Pilot Hill Wind, LLC (“Pilot Hill” and,

together with EDF Spring Field, Fox Squirrel, and Kelly Creek, the “PJM Project Companies”)

that will then be affiliates of the Purchaser will continue to be affiliated with less than one percent

of PJM’s installed capacity.13

            The Applicants’ PJM market presence is, and after closing will remain, de minimis. Based

on the text of the Application and the Solomon and Opgrand Affidavit, and the requirements of 18

C.F.R. § 2.26, the substance of which are not disputed by the IMM, the IMM Comments provides

no basis for the imposition of any non-standard condition on closing the Proposed Transaction.

           B.      The IMM has not Justified its Proposed Transaction-Specific Condition.

          The IMM requests a “commitment to not remove resources from the PJM markets to

directly serve data centers” by the PJM Project Companies.14 Section 203 permits the Commission

to impose a condition on a proposed transaction only when necessary to ensure that the transaction

is consistent with the public interest.15 No such condition is justified here because the Proposed

Transaction fully satisfies the standards set forth in the Commission’s regulations. The IMM

Comments identify no example of the Commission imposing requirements similar to what the

IMM seeks in this proceeding. The Proposed Transaction does not involve the failure of any

Commission competition standard, and therefore does not present any need for the imposition of

any competition-related condition16— particularly the unusual and previously-rejected condition


14
     IMM Comments at 6.
15

16
   See Inquiry Concerning the Comm’n’s Merger Pol’y Under the Fed. Power Act: Policy Statement, Order
No. 592, FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,044, at 30,118-30,119 (1996) (cross-referenced at 77 FERC ¶ 61,263),
reconsideration denied, Order No. 592-A, 79 FERC ¶ 61,321 (1997). The Commission has recently and
repeatedly rejected efforts by the IMM to secure unsupported behavioral mitigation conditions. See, e.g.,
KMC Thermo, LLC, et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,082, at P 65 (2026) (“With respect to the PJM IMM’s request
that the Commission impose behavioral commitments …, we decline to require the requested commitments
or to otherwise address general issues concerning the PJM markets in this proceeding. To challenge a
proposed transaction, a party must demonstrate that the proposed transaction will have an adverse effect on
horizontal competition, not that a proposed transaction must have some competitive benefit or market
enhancement. We find that the PJM IMM has not sufficiently demonstrated that the Proposed Transaction
would result in any adverse effect on competition to support the requested behavioral conditions. As the
Commission has previously found, arguments based on general concerns about certain elements of PJM’s
market design that are not specific to a proposed transaction under review are beyond the scope of the
Commission’s review of the proposed transaction. This proceeding, which only concerns the Proposed
Transaction, is not the appropriate venue for raising or addressing general concerns regarding market
design.”) (internal citations omitted); Algonquin Power Co., 189 FERC ¶ 61,214, at P 71 (2024) (rejecting
the IMM’s request in a Section 203 proceeding that the Commission impose behavioral mitigation

mitigation measures as a general matter” and “arguments based on general concerns about certain elements
of PJM’s market design that are not specific to a proposed transaction under review are beyond the scope
of the Commission’s review of the proposed transaction.”); Chalk Point Power, LLC, 189 FERC ¶ 61,042,
at P 30 (2024) (same); Clean Energy Future – Lordstown, LLC, 188 FERC ¶ 61,137, at P 44 (2024) (same);
Hunterstown Gen Holdings, LLC, 188 FERC ¶ 61,003, at P 42 (2024) (same); Energy Harbor Corp., 186

Section 203 proceedings involving PJM supports the same result here.18

          C.      The IMM’s Requested Relief Concerns Broader PJM Market Rules, not This
                  Transaction.

          The IMM seeks to use this Section 203 proceeding to obtain a transaction-specific solution

to an asserted gap in PJM’s generally applicable market rules, which are outside the scope of this

proceeding. Any such changes are appropriately addressed through PJM’s stakeholder process or

in a separate proceeding before the Commission. Indeed, the IMM itself acknowledges that

revising or supplementing PJM’s market rules falls outside the scope of this proceeding:

          The current rules in the PJM tariff do not explicitly address the removal of capacity
          resources from the capacity market to serve data center load. … The scope of this
          proceeding does not include revising or supplementing PJM’s market rules. The
          PJM market rules define the context within which the impact of the Transaction
          must be evaluated. The existing rules do not address or mitigate the potential
          adverse impact on competition from the removal of resources from the markets to
          serve data center loads . . . .19


17

Moreover, removal of the Hill Top Energy Center from the PJM market is governed by the PJM Tariff …
we conclude that any additional … requirements in this proceeding are not necessary.”) (internal citations

(setting aside a prior restriction imposing a notice requirement for the removal of a generator that was
acquired as part of a jurisdictional transaction).

             The Commission should therefore deny the IMM’s requested relief because this Section

203 proceeding is not the proper forum to revise or supplement PJM’s market rules. The IMM’s

Comments further demonstrate that relief it seeks stems from a broader disagreement with PJM

regarding the scope of PJM’s existing market rules. As the IMM acknowledges:

            Although the Market Monitor does not agree, PJM staff have publicly stated that
            the deactivation rules that define the PJM analysis and the Market Monitor analysis
            of proposed deactivations and their conclusions do not apply to the removal of
            resources to serve data center load.20

            The Commission should not resolve that broader disagreement between the IMM and PJM

over the PJM’s market rules by imposing the transaction-specific condition the IMM requests in

this Section 203 proceeding. The Commission should therefore decline the IMM’s invitation to

use this proceeding to resolve its broader disagreement with PJM.

            D.     The IMM’s Request for a Commitment Regarding “Direct” Sales is Unclear
                   and Unnecessary.

            The IMM repeatedly requests a commitment from “KKR Buyer”21 and/or from all

Applicants22 that the PJM Project Companies will not remove resources from the PJM markets to

serve data centers.23 That request is both undefined and unnecessary. The IMM does not explain

what it means by “direct” sales to a data center or how such a restriction would apply to the

wholesale sales the PJM Project Companies are authorized to make.

            More fundamentally, the IMM’s requested condition is unnecessary in light of the existing

legal limitations on the PJM Project Companies’ electricity sales activities. As the Application

 explains, EDF Spring Field is a wholesale power marketer; EDF Spring Field does not hold retail

power marketing authority.24 EDF Spring Field cannot and does not make retail sales.

          Similarly, the remaining PJM Project Companies are all EWGs under PUHCA.25 Under

the Commission’s regulations, an EWG must be “exclusively in the business of owning or

operating, or both owning and operating, all or part of one or more eligible facilities and selling

electric energy at wholesale” within the United States.26 The Commission’s regulations thus

already limit the PJM Project Companies to wholesale electric energy sales and they are prohibited

from making any retail sale of electricity, whether to a data center or otherwise.27 The IMM does

not explain what additional restriction its proposed prohibition on “direct” sales would impose

beyond these existing legal limitations, much less why that restriction is necessary to address a

purely hypothetical, transaction-specific competitive harm.          Accordingly, the IMM has not

established a basis for the Commission to impose the requested condition.

III.      REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ACTION AND AUTHORIZATION

          The Application demonstrates that the Proposed Transaction satisfies the requirements for

authorization under FPA Section 203, and the IMM Comments provide no basis to alter that

conclusion or delay Commission action. As demonstrated above, the IMM does not identify any

deficiency in the Application or any transaction-specific competitive harm that warrants further

review. Instead, the IMM’s concerns relate to broader issues concerning PJM’s market rules and

the potential future use of generation resources to serve data center load directly, none of which

the Applicants reiterate that consummation of the Proposed Transaction will not result in their PJM

market presence ceasing to be de minimis.

           Prompt Commission action also remains important to the timing of the Proposed

Transaction. As explained in the Application, Applicants must obtain approval from the French

Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial, Energy and Digital Sovereignty (“French

Ministry of Economy”) following receipt of all required North American regulatory approvals and

consents, including authorization under Section 203.28 Commission authorization is now the final

expected North American regulatory approval before the Applicants may seek the required French

Ministry of Economy approval, which is the final condition precedent to the consummation of the

Proposed Transaction. Accordingly, timely Commission action remains necessary to facilitate

Applicants’ efforts to obtain the French Ministry of Economy approval and consummate the

Proposed Transaction by December 21, 2026.

           Nothing in the IMM Comments warrants extending the Commission’s review or delaying

authorization of the Proposed Transaction. Applicants therefore respectfully renew their request

for expedited consideration and request that the Commission issue an order authorizing the

Proposed Transaction on or before November 20, 2026, or as soon thereafter as is practicable.

IV.        CONCLUSION

           As demonstrated in the Application and confirmed by the additional information provided

herein, the Proposed Transaction satisfies the Commission’s requirements for authorization under

Section 203 of the FPA. Accordingly, Applicants respectfully request that the Commission grant

leave to answer, accept this Answer, reject the arguments and requested relief set forth in the IMM

before November 20, 2026.
